##: The SDK is cloned once into the persist dir; installing another version only fetches that tag and checks it out. There is no usable download artifact, so 'url' is a placeholder and 'hash' is intentionally absent.
description: Flutter SDK with OpenHarmony/HarmonyOS support (CPF-Flutter fork), 3.41 maintenance line

script: Write-Host "Reusing the clone at $sdk; switching it to tag '$version' ..."
Write-Host 'Switching the existing clone failed; replacing it with a fresh shallow clone.' -ForegroundColor Yellow
if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { abort "git clone failed for tag '$version'" }

notes: The SDK lives once in ~/scoop/persist/flutter-ohos-341/sdk and is shared by every version of this package.
Installing or updating a version only fetches that tag (depth 1) and checks it out - no second clone, no duplicate SDK.
Because the checkout is shared, two versions cannot be live at once: the working tree follows whichever was installed last. 'flutter341 --version' reports the real one.
bin/cache artifacts survive a switch; Flutter re-downloads them when the engine revision differs.
scoop uninstall keeps the SDK; 'scoop uninstall flutter-ohos-341 --purge' deletes it.
Do NOT run 'flutter upgrade' - it pulls upstream Flutter and breaks the OH adapter.

autoupdate.note: Only the version changes: installer.script checks out that tag in the shared persist clone, and the download URL is a fixed placeholder. The repo's scripts/flutter-ohos-341.py applies the same rule (newest created_at, prereleases excluded) because the 3.41 line is tagged in two shapes across separate branches.
